question: Which of the keys held in the settings JSON of an organization (the per-capita rate and remittance day that set what it owes its parent body, the credit balance and renewal date that meter its use of metered features, the telephone number by which inbound text messages are attributed to it, branding, security policy and integration values) may the administrator of that organization write, which keys may only the platform operator or the parent body write, and which values must the software enforce when it saves them?
decision: Server-enforced allow-lists separate profile/branding/contact edits from financial rates, credit balance, inbound SMS assignment and security controls. Parent remittance rates require a verified parent-child relationship and authorized parent-body approval; platform billing ledger fields are changed through audited ledger operations, never direct JSON edits. Security options must be enforced by the actual identity/session control plane or withheld entirely from the UI; no decorative MFA/password policy fields.
originalProposedDecision: Allow-list per key. Org admin writes branding, contact and security policy. Platform operator only: credit balance, renewal date, inbound SMS number. Parent body only (confirmed affiliation): per-capita rate and remittance day. Security policy values (MFA, session timeout, password rules) are enforced at sign-in or removed from the page.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
